name: Parallel Projection Splatting with Bivariate Box Spline Footprint
definition: A volume rendering method for parallel projections where splats have identical shapes, differing only in color intensity and scale factor. It projects n-dimensional voxels (modeled as constant transparency cubes) onto 2D image space, using the luminosity distribution of a bivariate box spline.
summary: Parallel Projection Splatting with Bivariate Box Spline Footprint is a volume rendering technique that projects voxels using a reusable, scaled splat shape, avoiding the need for complex per-voxel footprint calculations or depth sorting.
